introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0560 History 1, June 2022, Ordinary Level, General Certificate of Education Board). One and a half hours. Answer ALL the 50 questions in this examination; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has FOUR suggested answers A, B, C and D: decide which answer is appropriate and mark only one answer for each question (if you mark more than one answer you score zero for that question). Use a soft HB pencil, avoid spending too much time on any one question, and do all rough work in the booklet. Mobile phones are not allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Page de garde verifiee : '0560 HISTORY 1', JUNE 2022, ORDINARY LEVEL, Multiple Choice Question Paper, One and a half hours, 'Answer ALL the 50 questions', toutes les questions de meme valeur. Aucune section a choix imprimee : regles_choix et groupes sont vides. Le sujet imprime n'indique aucun en-tete de section (Cameroun, Afrique, monde) ; seul l'ordre des themes le suggere.

Scan sans couche texte (5 pages, filigranes gcerevision.com ignores) lu page par page en image ; aucune figure, carte ni schema dans ce sujet : figures vide. Aucun calcul numerique, rien a recalculer avec Python.

Fautes d'impression laissees ou corrigees sans changer le sens : 'Arnet' (Arnett) laisse a la Q13, 'Marginot' (Maginot) laisse dans l'option de la Q47, 'Normady' (Normandy) a la Q34, 'Camerounaise' pour 'Camerounais' aux options de la Q17, 'Aveno' (Avenol) et 'Sean' (Sean Lester) a la Q49, 'Houphouet Biogny' et 'Aime Ceasar' aux Q39 et Q30, 'Liga' a l'option A de la Q45, 'Kellogg-Brain Pact' (Kellogg-Briand) a l'option C de la Q45 (laisse tel quel), 'Maji Resistance' (Maji Maji) a la Q28, 'in Kamerun' recopie a la Q8 ; Q5 imprimee 'Question 5 is based on...' recopiee 'This question is based on...'.

Q4 : aucune des quatre options imprimees (Rogozinski, Edward Schmidt, Johannes Voss, Nachtigal) n'est un agent britannique ; la bonne valeur (Edward Hewett) est absente des options. Question passee en OUVERTE, options recopiees dans l'enonce, reponse visee : Edward Hewett.

Q13 : le grief associe a la reforme du Resident E.J. Arnett (en poste dans les annees 1925-1932 d'apres les sources consultees) n'a pas pu etre etabli (les 4 options sont toutes plausibles : fermeture du Kake Teachers Training Centre, reduction du personnel medical de l'hopital de Victoria, frais medicaux eleves, abandon du chemin de fer). Aucune lettre choisie : question OUVERTE, reponse visee 'non etablie', a faire verifier par un historien ou dans le manuel.

Q23 : le congres de l'UNC qui a propose le poste de Premier ministre (cree en 1975, Paul Biya nomme le 30 juin 1975) n'a pas pu etre confirme ; l'attribution au Congres de Bamenda est la reponse vraisemblable des manuels mais non verifiee. Question passee en OUVERTE (reponse visee C, Bamenda, non verifiee).

Q25 : l'ajustement structurel a ete impose par le FMI et la Banque mondiale, deux institutions specialisees de l'ONU : les options C et D sont toutes deux defendables. Question passee en OUVERTE, reponse visee D (FMI), Banque mondiale mentionnee.
Q29 : le Kenya (reponse classique) et l'Afrique du Sud sont tous deux des colonies de peuplement blanc : options C et D defendables. Question passee en OUVERTE, reponse visee D (Kenya).

Converties en questions ouvertes (cle absente des options ou ambigue) : 4, 13, 23, 25, 29. Reponses visees : Q4 Edward Hewett, Q13 non etablie, Q23 C (Bamenda, non verifiee), Q25 D (FMI), Q29 D (Kenya). A relire par un historien.

Faits a marge d'incertitude (QCM conserves, cle deduite du programme et par elimination) : Q2 (premiere lettre formelle des chefs duala a la reine Victoria datee d'aout 1879 ; les dates de mars 1881-1883 sont des repetitions ou des distracteurs) ; Q3 (Max Buchner a bien accompagne Nachtigal en 1884, confirme ; la presence de 'Moebius' n'a pas pu etre verifiee, la paire B est la seule contenant Buchner) ; Q5 (lettre de Woermann a son agent Edward Schmidt ; Johannes Voss, agent de Jantzen et Thormaehlen, est le distracteur le plus proche) ; Q6 (les relations des Nso avec les Allemands ont varie : resistance puis cooperation ; la reponse Bamoun/Njoya est la plus sure) ; Q8 (premiere ligne : le Chemin de fer du Nord, Douala-Nkongsamba, commence en 1906, ouvert en 1911 ; la ligne du Centre date de 1908, mais 'premiere construite' depend du critere debut ou achevement des travaux) ; Q12 (1922 : confirmation des mandats par la SDN ; la vente des plantations allemandes a Londres eut aussi lieu en 1922 et 1924, mais l'option B n'est pas un changement administratif et politique) ; Q15 (13 sieges a l'Eastern House of Assembly d'Enugu, representation federale a Lagos non chiffree dans le corrige) ; Q16 (ministerial system et Premier Endeley en 1958 : date exacte non precisee dans le corrige) ; Q17 (BDC d'Aujoulat, 1951 ; le Democrates Camerounais de Mbida est un autre parti modere de la meme periode, dont la date de creation n'est pas precisee) ; Q18 (l'enonce dit 1944 : l'USCC date de 1944, la greve et les emeutes de Douala de septembre 1945 ; formulation prudente dans le corrige) ; Q19 (Foumban, juillet 1961 ; la conference tripartite de Yaounde d'aout 1961 a aussi traite de la constitution) ; Q21 (crise du KNDP : le corrige ne date pas la crise plus precisement que 'early 1960s') ; Q24 (7 provinces a 10 en 1983 ; les totaux de 58 divisions et 360 arrondissements ne sont pas dates dans le corrige) ; Q36 (Algerie et Kenya : 'bloodiest' est une exageration car l'Angola et le Mozambique furent aussi tres sanglants, mais la paire C est la seule acceptable) ; Q38 (l'enonce dit 1961, la secession du Katanga date de juillet 1960 ; signale dans le corrige) ; Q44 (Italie, 1915 ; 'tilted the course' est une exageration de l'enonce) ; Q47 (contournement de la ligne Maginot par les Ardennes, cause classique) ; Q50 (D : l'ONU ne 'reconnait' pas le terrorisme, elle le condamne).

Seconde passe faite : les 5 pages du PDF ont ete relues en image et les 50 questions resolues une deuxieme fois independamment ; enonces et options conformes au sujet (hors fautes d'impression signalees).

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following coastal towns of Cameroon owes its creation in the 1850s to the activities of the English Baptist Missionaries?
questions.corrige_markdown: Victoria (today Limbe) was founded in 1858 by the English Baptist missionary Alfred Saker of the Baptist Missionary Society. After the Spanish authorities in Fernando Po restricted Protestant missions, Saker settled a group of converts and freed slaves at the foot of Mount Cameroon and named the town after Queen Victoria. Douala, Bimbia and Edea were already African settlements before the missionaries came: they were not created by the Baptist missionaries. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which month and year did the Cameroon kings and chiefs make a formal request to the British monarch to annex Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Duala kings and chiefs (notably King Bell and King Akwa) first wrote formally to Queen Victoria in August 1879 asking Britain to take over their country and to protect their trade and their authority. Because London did not give a clear answer, they repeated the request in later letters, but the first formal request is the one dated August 1879. The three other dates are later repetitions of the request. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following pairs of German officials accompanied Gustav Nachtigal on his mission to annex Cameroon in 1884?
questions.corrige_markdown: Gustav Nachtigal, the German Imperial Commissioner, sailed to West Africa in 1884 on the gunboat Moewe to place Togo and Cameroon under German protection. Dr Max Buchner, who stayed on as deputy to the Imperial Commissioner in Cameroon, accompanied him, together with Moebius, so the pair in option B is the one that fits. Woermann and Schmidt were traders (Adolph Woermann was the Hamburg shipowner and Schmidt his agent in Douala), not officials of the mission. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Below is a list of European agents who signed treaties of annexation in Cameroon. The name of the British agent who committed himself to sign treaties with the coastal chiefs after 1884 was ...

*Options as printed:* A) Rogozinski   B) Edward Schmidt   C) Johannes Voss   D) Gustav Nachtigal
questions.corrige_markdown:
The British agent concerned was Edward Hewett, British Consul for the Bights of Benin and Biafra. He was sent to the Cameroon coast to make treaties with the Duala chiefs and place the area under British protection, as the chiefs had asked in 1879, but he arrived a few days after the Germano-Duala treaty of 12 July 1884 had been signed, so Britain lost the race and Cameroon became a German protectorate. None of the four printed options is a British agent: Rogozinski was a Polish explorer active near Mount Cameroon, Edward Schmidt and Johannes Voss were agents of German trading firms in Douala, and Gustav Nachtigal was the German Imperial Commissioner.

**Intended answer: Edward Hewett (British Consul).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: This question is based on the confidential instructions by a Hamburg trader on the eve of the German annexation of Cameroon: "If you present things properly to these chiefs, I do not have any doubt that you will be successful ... The Cameroons must become German before the English have an inkling of it ..." Identify the agent of the Woermann Firm in Cameroon to whom the letter was addressed.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Hamburg trader was Adolph Woermann, head of the Woermann firm, who wrote to his agent in Douala, Edward (Eduard) Schmidt, urging him to obtain treaties from the Duala chiefs before the British could act. Adolf and Carl Woermann belonged to the Hamburg family firm itself, so they cannot be the agent to whom the letter was sent, and Johannes Voss was the agent of the other Hamburg firm, Jantzen and Thormaehlen. Schmidt and Voss later witnessed the Germano-Duala treaty of 12 July 1884. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these Cameroonian tribes remained loyal to the Germans between 1890 and 1914?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Bamoun (Bamum) kingdom under King Njoya cooperated with the Germans throughout the colonial period: Njoya accepted German protection, used German support to strengthen his rule and kept friendly relations until 1914. The Bakweri (who resisted the Germans on the slopes of Mount Cameroon in the early 1890s), the Nso and the Bangwa all resisted German penetration at different times. **Answer: B.**
themes: indigenous resistance to german rule in cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these was the first Catholic missionary body to arrive Cameroon in 1890?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Pallotine Fathers (a German Catholic society) landed in Cameroon in 1890 and opened their first mission at Douala, then spread inland. The Holy Ghost Fathers took over in French Cameroon only after the Germans were expelled during the First World War, the Mill Hill Fathers came to British Southern Cameroons in 1922, and the Baptist Missionary Society was a Protestant body that had arrived in the 1840s. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The name of the first railway line constructed by the Germans in Kamerun was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Germans began the Northern Railway (Douala-Nkongsamba) in 1906 and opened it as far as Nkongsamba in 1911, to carry the plantation produce of the Mount Cameroon and Moungo areas to the port of Douala. The Midland Railway from Douala towards Yaounde was started later (1908) and had reached only about Eseka when the war broke out in 1914; the rest of the line to Yaounde was finished by the French in the 1920s. There was no Douala-Edea railway. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The German explorer who signed a blood pact with Fon Galega I of Bali was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Eugen Zintgraff, a German explorer and colonial agent, explored the grassland of Cameroon in the late 1880s and made a blood pact with Fon Galega I of Bali, which gave him a friendly base for his expeditions and for trade. Nachtigal annexed the coast in 1884 and is not linked with the Bali pact, and Morgan and Tappenberg are not the explorer associated with it. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following European capital cities hosted the signing ceremony of the Milner-Simon Agreement that confirmed the 1916 Anglo-French provisional partition of Cameroon?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Milner-Simon Agreement was signed in London on 10 July 1919 by Lord Milner, the British Colonial Secretary, and Henri Simon, the French Minister for the Colonies. It confirmed the provisional division of Cameroon agreed in 1916, with France receiving about four-fifths of the territory and Britain the strips along the Nigerian border. The agreement was later given legal form by the League of Nations mandates of 1922. **Answer: B.**
themes: partition of cameroon after world war one

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the battle of the First World War in Cameroon in which the German Commander Colonel Zimmermann suffered defeat and escaped to Spanish Equatorial Guinea.
questions.corrige_markdown: After the Allies took Douala (September 1914), the German commander Colonel Carl Zimmermann withdrew inland to Yaounde. When Allied columns closed in on Yaounde in late 1915 and early 1916, the Germans were defeated there and retreated south; Zimmermann and most of his troops crossed into Spanish Guinea (Rio Muni) in early 1916, where they were interned. Nsanakang (1914) was a German success against the British, and the German garrison at Mora in the north was the last to surrender, in February 1916. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Of what significance was the year 1922 in the administrative and political development of the British Southern Cameroons during the Mandate period?
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1922 the Council of the League of Nations confirmed the division of Cameroon into a British and a French mandate (Class B mandates), so British Southern Cameroons formally became a British mandate territory, administered as part of Nigeria. Option D is wrong because the German administrators had been driven out by 1916, option C confuses the mandate with Lord Lugard's theory of the dual mandate, which was not started in Cameroon, and option B describes an economic measure (the sale of former German plantations by the British authorities), not the constitutional change asked about. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: British Southern Cameroon became a British mandate
Auction sale of German plantations was launched
Dual mandate in British Tropical Africa started in Cameroon

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following reforms was associated with the British Resident E.J. Arnet that made him unpopular with the indigenous population?

*Options as printed:* A) The closure of the Kake Teachers Training Centre   B) The reduction of medical staff of Victoria hospital   C) The high medical fees in hospitals   D) The abandonment of railway development
questions.corrige_markdown:
E.J. Arnett served as British Resident in charge of the Cameroons Province in the second half of the 1920s and the early 1930s. The reform that made him unpopular with the people is not established by the sources that could be checked for this solution, and the four printed options are all plausible local grievances of the mandate period, so no option is marked as correct. The question is therefore left open for self-assessment and should be checked in the history textbook used in class (Southern Cameroons under the British mandate).

**Intended answer: not established.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The indigenes of French Cameroon opposed French colonial policy of "la mise en valeur" because ...
questions.corrige_markdown: La mise en valeur was the French programme of developing the economic resources of the colony (roads, railways, plantations). It was carried out largely with African labour that was unpaid or badly paid: every adult male had to give ten days of free labour a year (the prestation) and many were also recruited for road and railway gangs, which the people hated. Imprisonment without trial and the division of people into citizens and subjects belong to the indigenat system, and option D only restates the policy without giving a reason for opposition. **Answer: B.**
themes: french rule in cameroon under the mandate

choix.texte: It led to imprisonment without trial
It led to ten days of free labour
It classified the people into citizens and subjects
It enforced development to ease exploitation of resources

questions.enonce_markdown: The Macpherson Constitution of 1951 was important to the British Southern Cameroons because it gave the territory ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Under the Macpherson Constitution of 1951, Southern Cameroons, still part of the Eastern Region of Nigeria, was given 13 seats in the Eastern House of Assembly at Enugu, a clear increase over its earlier representation, and it was also represented at the federal level. Quasi-federal status with its own House of Assembly in Buea came only later, with the Lyttelton Constitution of 1954. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: 13 seats in the Eastern House of Assembly at Enugu
2 seats in the Eastern House of Assembly at Enugu
1 seat in the Legislative Council in Lagos
Quasi federal status with a House of Assembly in Buea

questions.enonce_markdown: The "ministerial system of government" was introduced in the British Southern Cameroons in 1958 for the first time by ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Dr E.M.L. Endeley, leader of the Kamerun National Congress (KNC), headed the government of Southern Cameroons in the late 1950s: he was Leader of Government Business after 1954 and became the first Premier when the ministerial system of government was introduced in 1958. J.N. Foncha of the KNDP replaced him as Premier after winning the elections of January 1959. S.T. Muna and P.M. Kale were other politicians of the period but did not head the government at that time. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which political party was formed to counter the growing popularity of the UPC Party in French Cameroon in the early 1950s?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Bloc Democratique Camerounais (BDC) was founded in 1951 by Louis-Paul Aujoulat, a French politician close to the colonial administration, as a moderate party meant to weaken the radical UPC (founded in 1948). The Union Camerounaise was formed later, in 1958, by Ahmadou Ahidjo. The Democrates Camerounais of Andre-Marie Mbida were another moderate group of the same years, but the BDC is the party usually quoted as set up against the UPC.  **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which trade union in French Cameroon spearheaded the 1944 strikes that resulted in the deaths of some people?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Union des Syndicats Confederes du Cameroun (USCC), created in 1944 with the help of French trade unionists such as Gaston Donnat, organised the workers' strikes of Douala; the strike of September 1945 ended in riots in which a number of people were killed. The other three names are not the union that led these events. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In which of the following post 1961 plebiscite conferences was a federal form of the Cameroon state adopted?
questions.corrige_markdown: After the plebiscite of February 1961, the leaders of Southern Cameroons and of the Republic of Cameroon met at Foumban in July 1961 to draw up the constitution of the new state; the federal form of government (the Federal Republic of Cameroon, with two federated states) was adopted there. The Mamfe Conference (1959) belongs to the period before the plebiscite, and the Bamenda Conference (June 1961) was the meeting of Southern Cameroons leaders that prepared their proposals before Foumban. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Below are colleges set up in the 1960s in Cameroon. Identify the name of the college which was set up in West Cameroon to promote the bilingual nature of West Cameroonians.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Government Bilingual Grammar School, Molyko-Buea, was opened in 1963 in the Federated State of West Cameroon to teach English-speaking pupils in both official languages, as part of the policy of building a bilingual nation. The Bilingual Practising School belongs to Yaounde, in East Cameroon, the College of Arts, Science and Technology at Bambili is a college of general and technical education that was not created for bilingualism, and Government Grammar School Mamfe is an ordinary English-medium school. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Cameroon College of Arts, Science and Technology, Bambili

questions.enonce_markdown: "Foncha is the number 1 devil and Nzo Ekahnghaky is the number 2 devil in the party." This statement refers to the party crisis which rocked West Cameroon politics in the early 1960s in the ...
questions.corrige_markdown: John Ngu Foncha was the founder and leader of the Kamerun National Democratic Party (KNDP) and Nzo Ekangaki was its secretary general, so a remark describing them as the number 1 and the number 2 devil in the party can only refer to a crisis inside the KNDP, the ruling party of West Cameroon. The CPNC (Endeley and Mukete) and the KUP (Kale) were opposition parties of that period. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following was created by the Ahidjo administration to promote the cultivation of rubber?
questions.corrige_markdown: HEVECAM (Hevea Cameroun) was set up in 1975 as a state company to grow and process rubber (hevea), first at Niete in the South. CICAM is the textile company, ALUCAM the aluminium smelter at Edea and SODECAO the cocoa development company. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In which CNU congress was the proposal made to amend the constitution of the United Republic of Cameroon to create the post of the Prime Minister?

*Options as printed:* A) Douala Congress   B) Bafoussam Congress   C) Bamenda Congress   D) Yaounde Congress
questions.corrige_markdown:
The post of Prime Minister was created by the constitutional amendment of 1975, and Paul Biya was appointed to it on 30 June 1975. The proposal is attributed in the school textbooks to the Bamenda Congress of the Cameroon National Union (CNU), the single party founded in 1966. The sources that could be checked for this solution confirm the creation of the post in 1975 but not the congress, so the question is left open and the congress named here should be checked in the textbook.

**Intended answer: C (Bamenda Congress), not independently verified.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: In 1983 President Paul Biya reorganized the administrative map of Cameroon by ...
questions.corrige_markdown: In 1983 the Great North was split into three provinces (Adamawa, North and Far North) and the Centre-South into Centre and South, so the number of provinces rose from seven to ten. The states of East and West Cameroon had already been abolished in 1972, when the unitary state was created, and the totals of 58 divisions and about 360 subdivisions describe later administrative divisions and not the 1983 reform. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Increasing the number of divisions to 58.
Increasing the number of provinces from seven to ten.
Abolishing the states of East and West Cameroon.
Increasing the number of subdivisions to 360.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the following specialized agencies of the UNO imposed the Structural Adjustment Programme on Cameroon to resolve the economic crisis of the 1980s?

*Options as printed:* A) UNESCO   B) FAO   C) World Bank   D) IMF
questions.corrige_markdown:
When Cameroon's economy collapsed in the second half of the 1980s (falling prices of cocoa, coffee and oil, heavy debt), the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank both demanded a Structural Adjustment Programme: cuts in public spending, salary reductions, privatisation and a reduction of the civil service. The IMF is usually named as the agency that imposed it, but the World Bank also took part and is also a specialized agency of the United Nations, so options C and D are both defensible. UNESCO (education and culture) and FAO (food and agriculture) played no such role.

**Intended answer: D (IMF), with the World Bank as a partner.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: Liberia and Abyssinia during the scramble for Africa had one thing in common. The common element was that ...
questions.corrige_markdown: During the scramble for Africa, Liberia (founded by freed American slaves and independent since 1847) and Abyssinia (Ethiopia, which defeated Italy at Adowa in 1896) were the only two African states that kept their independence. Liberia was never colonized by the USA nor attacked by Italy, and the League of Nations question concerns only Ethiopia in 1935. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: They were all colonized by the USA
They were all victims of Italian aggression
They were the only independent African states
The League of Nations refused to assist them when they faced European aggression

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following European countries was among the last to join the colonial scramble for Africa but lost her colonies by 1919?
questions.corrige_markdown: Germany entered the scramble late, after 1884 (Togo, Cameroon, South West Africa and East Africa), and lost all its colonies after defeat in the First World War: by the Treaty of Versailles of 1919 they were taken away and placed under League of Nations mandates held by the victors. France, Belgium and Britain kept their colonies. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The scorch earth policy used in West Africa between the 1880s and 1890s as a method of resistance was adopted in the ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Samori Toure, the ruler of the Mandinka empire in West Africa, used a scorched earth policy against the French in the 1890s: as he withdrew he burnt villages and destroyed crops so that the advancing French troops could find no food. Opobo resisted through trade and diplomacy under Jaja, Abyssinia through a modern army, and the Maji Maji rising (the "Maji Resistance" of option D) took place in German East Africa in 1905, not in West Africa. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of these African territories served as a typical white settler colony?

*Options as printed:* A) Sierra Leone   B) Ivory Coast   C) South Africa   D) Kenya
questions.corrige_markdown:
A white settler colony was a colony in which large numbers of Europeans settled permanently, took the best farm land and held political power. Kenya is the classic East African example (European farmers on the White Highlands, which led to the Mau Mau revolt), and South Africa is also a settler territory, while Sierra Leone and the Ivory Coast, in West Africa, had only small European populations of officials and traders. Because both Kenya and South Africa fit the description, the question is left open.

**Intended answer: D (Kenya), South Africa also being a settler colony.**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The African elite who symbolized the success of the French policy of assimilation and served in the French government during the inter-war period was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Blaise Diagne of Senegal, one of the "evolues" of the Four Communes, became in 1914 the first African deputy in the French National Assembly and later held a post in the French government (Under-Secretary of State for the Colonies in 1931). He is the symbol of the assimilation policy between the wars. Senghor and Houphouet-Boigny entered the French government after the Second World War, and Aime Cesaire was a poet and politician from Martinique, not from Africa. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following describe the British Colonial policy of Indirect Rule **EXCEPT:**
questions.corrige_markdown: Indirect rule meant governing the Africans through their own chiefs and political institutions under the supervision of British officials; where there was no chief (as among the Igbo of Nigeria) the British appointed warrant chiefs. Ruling through British traders was never part of the system, so it is the exception. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Rule through the African traditional rulers
Governing the Africans through traditional political structure
Governing the African people through warrant chiefs appointed by the British

questions.enonce_markdown: The African territory which as a result of her participation in the First World War was mandated to South Africa during the Paris Peace Treaty was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: South Africa fought on the Allied side in the First World War and conquered the German colony of South West Africa (today Namibia) in 1915; after the war the League of Nations gave it to South Africa as a mandate. Ruanda-Urundi went to Belgium, Togoland was divided between Britain and France and Tanganyika went to Britain. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the group of Africans whose participation in the First World War empowered them for African nationalism.
questions.corrige_markdown: African soldiers who fought in the First World War, in Europe and in Africa, saw that white men could be defeated and killed, learnt about freedom and self-determination and often returned with new skills and the wish for better treatment; many of the ex-servicemen became leaders or supporters of the nationalist movements. **Answer: A.**
themes: impact of world war one on africa

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the name of a major battle fought during the Second World War in North Africa by the Allied forces.
questions.corrige_markdown: The Battle of El-Alamein in Egypt (1942) was fought in North Africa between British and Commonwealth forces under General Montgomery and the German-Italian army of Rommel, and it was a turning point of the war in Africa. Stalingrad was fought in Russia, Normandy (1944) in France and the Battle of Britain in the air over Britain. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The Pan African Congress held after the Second World War that requested the use of force in the nationalist struggle in Africa was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: The Fifth Pan-African Congress, held in Manchester in October 1945 and attended by Kwame Nkrumah, Jomo Kenyatta and W.E.B. Du Bois, declared that Africans would use force if necessary to win their freedom, since peaceful methods had not worked. The earlier congresses had been held in Paris, Brussels and London, and none was held in Lisbon. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the pair of African states whose wars of nationalism were the bloodiest in Africa.
questions.corrige_markdown: Algeria (the war against France, 1954-1962) and Kenya (the Mau Mau revolt against the British, 1952-1960) are the pair in which the struggle for independence caused the greatest violence among the options; both had large European settler populations who refused to give up power. Uganda, Rwanda and Nigeria gained independence largely by negotiation, and Nigeria's path was peaceful. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Name the Nigerian political party whose leader became the first Prime Minister of the Federation at independence in 1960.
questions.corrige_markdown: At independence in October 1960 the first Prime Minister of the Federation of Nigeria was Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa, the leader of the Northern Peoples Congress (NPC), the party that won the most seats in the federal elections. The Action Group was led by Awolowo, the NCNC by Azikiwe, and the "Northern Peoples Union" was not the name of a party. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: National Council of Nigeria and Cameroons

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following Congolese leaders attempted secession of Katanga from the rest of Congo in 1961 leading to the outbreak of the civil war?
questions.corrige_markdown: Moise Tshombe, leader of Katanga province and supported by Belgian mining interests, proclaimed the secession of Katanga from the Congo (the declaration came just after independence, in 1960, and the secession lasted until 1963). Patrice Lumumba was the first Prime Minister, Joseph Kasavubu the first President, and Simon Kimbangu was an earlier religious leader of the colonial period. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Name the African leader who provided aid to Guinea-Conakry when the French withdrew all forms of aid in 1958.
questions.corrige_markdown: Guinea voted "No" in the referendum of 1958 and became independent under Sekou Toure; France withdrew its officials and aid at once. Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana came to its help with financial aid (a loan) and political support, and the two countries announced a union. Houphouet-Boigny, who favoured links with France, did not help, and Azikiwe and Olympio were not the leaders who gave this aid. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following African countries organized the first summit of the OAU in 1963?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Organisation of African Unity was founded at Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, in May 1963 and Emperor Haile Selassie hosted the first summit; the OAU headquarters were set up in the same city. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The industrialisation of European economies in the 1870s had its origin from ...
questions.corrige_markdown: Industrialisation began in Britain, where the Industrial Revolution started in the late eighteenth century (coal, iron, steam engines and textile factories). Belgium, France and Germany industrialised later, copying British methods, and by the 1870s German and other European industries were rivalling Britain's. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: As a result of the Peace Treaty of Versailles, France recovered from Germany ...
questions.corrige_markdown: By the Treaty of Versailles (1919) Germany gave back Alsace and Lorraine, which it had taken from France in 1871 after the Franco-Prussian War. France also received control of the coal mines of the Saar for fifteen years, but the Ruhr stayed German (France occupied it only in 1923), the Rhineland was demilitarised, and the Polish Corridor went to Poland. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following European Alliances guaranteed the security of France against Germany in 1907?
questions.corrige_markdown: The Triple Entente was formed in 1907, when Britain and Russia settled their differences and joined France, which was already linked with Britain (Entente Cordiale, 1904) and Russia (1894); it protected France against the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy. The Entente Cordiale (1904) was an agreement between only two powers, and the Dual Alliance was the German-Austrian alliance of 1879. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the Great Power whose entry into the First World War in 1915 tilted the course of the War in favour of the Allied Powers.
questions.corrige_markdown: Italy, which had been a member of the Triple Alliance but stayed neutral in 1914, joined the Allies in 1915 after the Treaty of London and attacked Austria-Hungary, forcing the Central Powers to fight on one more front. The USA joined only in 1917, Russia had been in the war since 1914, and Japan entered in 1914. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following treaties signed in the 1920s paved the way for the admission of Germany into the League of Nations in 1926?
questions.corrige_markdown: By the Locarno Treaties of 1925 Germany, France and Belgium accepted their common frontiers and Britain and Italy guaranteed them; this restored confidence in Germany, which was then admitted to the League of Nations in 1926. The Kellogg-Briand Pact (1928) renounced war, and the Treaty of Brest-Litovsk (1918) was imposed by Germany on Russia. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An important **economic** effect of the First World War on European economies which resulted in a sharp fall in the value of currencies was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: To pay for the war the governments borrowed heavily and printed money, and the shortage of goods raised prices: this galloping inflation made currencies lose value sharply (in Germany it ended in the hyperinflation of 1923). Unemployment, falling trade and falling exports were effects of the war, but they are not the direct cause of a fall in the value of money. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: A decline in inter European trade

questions.enonce_markdown: The main reason for the rapid fall of France in 1940 was ...
questions.corrige_markdown: In May 1940 the German army avoided the strongly fortified Maginot Line on the Franco-German frontier and attacked through the Ardennes and Belgium, using fast tank columns and air power (blitzkrieg), so the French defences were outflanked and France asked for an armistice in June. British help was limited but was not the main cause, Russia was at that time bound to Germany by the 1939 pact, and Mussolini attacked France only in June 1940, when the defeat was already certain. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: German avoidance of the Marginot Line

questions.enonce_markdown: Identify the United Nations Agency which was created to cater for the welfare of children throughout the world.
questions.corrige_markdown: UNICEF (the United Nations Children's Fund) was created in 1946 to help children in need, first the child victims of the Second World War, and now children everywhere. UNESCO deals with education, science and culture, WHO with health and FAO with food and agriculture. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Who was the first Secretary General of the League of Nations?
questions.corrige_markdown: Sir Eric Drummond, a British diplomat, was the first Secretary General of the League of Nations (1920-1933). Joseph Avenol, a Frenchman, succeeded him, Sean Lester was the last Secretary General, and Albert Thomas was the first Director of the International Labour Office. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Terrorism is difficult to combat because of the following **EXCEPT:**
questions.corrige_markdown: Terrorism is hard to fight because it is often supported from abroad, because the attackers strike suddenly and disappear (hit and run), and because suicide bombers cannot be deterred by the threat of punishment. The United Nations does not recognize terrorism: it condemns it, so this statement is not a reason why terrorism is difficult to combat. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: It operates hit and run tactics
It is recognized by the UN
